events.title: Refund Operations | achopikyan
events.copy: One source dataset, two workspaces. Current v1 reproduces the old policy in a simulated ledger. v2 and v3 are tested before release.

events.title: Reviewer: all 20 supplied requests
events.copy: All includes completed automatic refunds. Open, Fraud Review, Waiting and Completed are separate filters.

events.title: A workspace for fast, careful reviews
events.copy: The queue stays on the left. Each request has separate sections, with distinct colors and a persistent action bar.

events.title: Correct the request where you read it
events.copy: Structured fields can be corrected with an explanation. Saving a changed input invalidates its old analysis and prepares new evidence.

events.title: Trace every applicable rule
events.copy: The Current version, route and reason appear together. All enabled rules are evaluated; priorities and policy-wide checks resolve the outcome.

events.title: LLM extraction is already prepared
events.copy: The model reads request-time context and notes, extracts predefined facts, and cites source text. It does not approve refunds or see future outcomes.

events.title: Risk supports judgment
events.copy: Historical cohorts and monetary scenarios show recorded chargebacks, missing outcomes, review cost and possible exposure. Scenario assumptions remain explicit.

events.title: Customer context stays separate
events.copy: Earlier requests, prior refunds and inconsistent source data are visible. Activity records changes and decisions without cluttering the main review.

events.title: An audit trail for every action
events.copy: Approvals, partial refunds, rejection, requests for information, fraud escalation and holds are explained and recorded.

events.title: Conflicting source rows cannot silently become a payment
events.copy: RF-2183 contains two amounts. A reviewer must verify the canonical version; the system keeps both originals and blocks an unresolved approval.

events.title: Manager: one library of policy versions
events.copy: v1 remains Current. v2 and v3 start as editable drafts; each has its own Settings, Rules, Discovery, Backtest and Shadow pages.

events.title: Create a version from an existing policy or from scratch
events.copy: Creation is explicit. Editing an existing draft autosaves that same version; it does not create another policy.

events.title: Visible checks and editable limits
events.copy: Data safety, business checks, standard evidence questions and payment budgets are explicit. No hidden fallback rule decides a refund.

events.title: Edit rules in place, with autosave
events.copy: Change a condition directly and see it save. We restore the original $300 threshold before Backtest so comparisons use the supplied versions.

events.title: Two ways to add a rule
events.copy: Build manually, or describe an intent and review the LLM proposal before adding it. Natural-language drafting needs a live connection; this recording uses saved evidence.

events.title: Discover new hypotheses from historical cases
events.copy: Candidates not already covered by this version show support, manual-review opportunity, unknown outcomes and financial scenarios. Selection has a clear destination.

events.title: Inspect evidence before adding a candidate
events.copy: Training support and a later diagnostic split are shown separately. Historical approvals are observations, not ground-truth safety labels.

events.title: Backtest: inspect the plan before running
events.copy: Every historical request is replayed through this exact version using its saved extraction. Outcomes remain diagnostic context and replay makes no payments.

events.title: v2: historical results for this version
events.copy: The page reports v2 alone. The manager sees routing, evidence completeness and uncertainty before deciding whether to begin Shadow.

events.title: Safety & evidence
events.copy: Known adverse outcomes, missing evidence and unobserved outcomes remain distinct. Zero recorded errors does not prove zero risk.

events.title: Workload & money
events.copy: Proposed refund exposure, historical review minutes and assumption-based costs reveal tradeoffs. Proposed money is not money actually paid.

events.title: Segments & rules
events.copy: Inspect where results change by cohort and which rules match, win, or are overridden. Aggregate automation can hide a risky segment.

events.title: Cases
events.copy: Only Cases expands individual requests. Inspect disagreements and supporting evidence before treating a metric as a release argument.

events.title: Shadow starts only when the manager chooses
events.copy: Backtest does not silently activate Shadow. The version is frozen before observing the shared request pool.

events.title: v2 is now in Shadow
events.copy: It evaluates the same existing requests as Current, without creating payments or showing its proposals to reviewers. Existing backlog cannot qualify a release.

events.title: v3: a deliberately broader alternative
events.copy: v3 allows larger apparel returns, including repeat requests. It is a hypothesis to investigate, not an improvement just because it automates more.

events.title: v3 follows the same historical checks
events.copy: The same data, saved evidence and evaluation engine make version differences inspectable. No special evaluation mode favors a candidate.

events.title: Both candidates now observe the shared pool
events.copy: v1 is still Current. v2 and v3 are in Shadow, with locked rules and separate results.

events.title: One independent reviewer decision
events.copy: The reviewer sees Current and source evidence only. This partial-refund decision will become a shared comparison reference for both Shadow versions.

events.title: A recorded decision and one simulated payment
events.copy: The decision is versioned, explained and written atomically with its ledger entry. Repeating the action cannot create a second refund.

events.title: Missing evidence has a real work state
events.copy: The request waits for information. It cannot proceed until new evidence is recorded and verified; fraud escalation and holds use the same explicit workflow.

events.title: Compare all three versions on the same history
events.copy: Current v1, v2 and v3 appear side by side. Each indicator keeps its denominator and definition; the manager owns the acceptable tradeoff.

events.title: More automation is not the whole decision
events.copy: Compare review workload alongside refund exposure, known adverse outcomes and missing outcome coverage. Cost assumptions are editable in global Settings.

events.title: Shadow comparison reuses the reviewer work
events.copy: The same request pool and the recorded partial decision feed both candidates. Agreement, changed decisions and potential overpayment remain visible per version.

events.title: A demonstration is not prospective release evidence
events.copy: The source backlog cannot prove a safe rollout. Activation stays unavailable until the configured new-arrival evidence and financial requirements are met.

events.title: Current performance belongs to the serving version
events.copy: Open workload, recorded decisions, actual simulated payments, outcomes and execution limits are separated. v1 stayed Current throughout this walkthrough.

events.title: Current runs automatically within visible limits
events.copy: Each eligible payment checks data, evidence, amount and cumulative spending atomically. A blocked case stays available for human review.

events.title: Run the supplied file or import another CSV
events.copy: The same application supports pending.csv and a new file with the same columns. Imports preserve source rows, normalize values and surface duplicates.

events.title: One local app, two operating systems
events.copy: Windows: START.cmd. macOS: sh START.command. The launcher installs dependencies and opens the browser. API keys stay on the backend.

events.title: Ready for an evidence-based decision | achopikyan
events.copy: v1 Current. v2 and v3 in Shadow. Real saved extraction, explainable rules and explicit uncertainty; no fabricated prospective outcomes or real payments.
